title: TextureProgressBar transform origin snaps to nearest pixel when resized
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduced in 4.7.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun, 24 May 2026 04:47:00 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX Vega (RADV VEGA10) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.26 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When scaling a TextureProgressBar with an offset pivot (either ratio or pixel value), it jumps about the pivot point, snapping to the nearest pixel. This doesn't occur when rotating.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd763873-5aa5-4b6d-b3da-b561ea62d440

@kleonc has found this to be related to `gui/common/snap_controls_to_pixels` project setting (enabled by default). Disabling it makes the jitter go away. 

The issue seems to be the transform origin is being rounded down, but the TextureProgressBar's drawing logic acts as if it was still centered without snapping.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f964fa714f503bd063b96f6194eb3e45355c1084/scene/gui/control.cpp#L789-L792

Zoomed in with the pixel grid visible:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35e237c2-61cd-4201-bb38-b7ff07898e70

### Steps to reproduce

Scale a TextureProgressBar when it has an offset pivot.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[scaling-pivot-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29175266/scaling-pivot-repro.zip)
